answer: Prior art is the Bayes reject option (Chow 1970), deep selective classification (SelectiveNet Table 2), selective QA under domain shift (Kamath 56.1% vs MaxProb 48.2% coverage at 80% accuracy), and on-demand retrieval (Self-RAG PopQA 54.9 vs Llama2-7B no-retrieve 14.7 / always-retrieve 38.2). RouteLLM cuts cost between models (3.66x vs random 2.49x at 95% GPT-4) but does not implement null injection. Recommended cutoff under assumed C_wrong:C_miss=4:1 is tau=0.75; inverted 1:4 yields tau=0, where abstention is strictly worse than always answering. SUCCESS:RES-0103 in the receipt AND a threshold recommendation with an explicit cost-ratio assumption and an inverted-ratio sensitivity
canonical_mechanism: Chow reject option on router confidence: inject only when s > 1 - C_miss/C_wrong; otherwise inject nothing
completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:RES-0103 in the receipt AND a threshold recommendation with an explicit cost-ratio assumption and an inverted-ratio sensitivity

contradiction_edges.note: Judge abstention assumes a wrong score is worse than leaving an item unscored. Capability routing often has the opposite ratio.
RouteLLM never selects the null injection.

control_regime.demonstration: inverted always-answer cost=36; tau=0.75 cost=240; strictly_worse=True
control_regime.when_abstention_strictly_worse: Whenever C_miss >= C_wrong (inverted 1:4 here), any tau>0 is strictly more expensive than always answering on the fixture, because abstaining pays C_miss with certainty while injecting pays C_wrong only on errors, and C_wrong <= C_miss.
